risk_note: Gate tooling only (FU-VERIFY-FAST-PROFILE, D10-2503 / D10-2504). tools/ci/fast-parts.ts derives the parts of verify:fast as CI runs them - base (the trusted package.json verify:fast steps, its `pnpm run test` replaced by the verify-unit turbo command) and spec-1..N (the verify-spec-<i> shard commands) - and refuses (exit 2) unless the three together run exactly the set of the whole verify:fast: one root test step, a root test script that is a plain turbo run test, verify-unit adding exactly one exclusion of the package the spec parts run, shards 1..N each once. Every run step of those CI jobs must equal an entry of a trusted allow list character for character (two anchored templates with a strict package name and positive integers for the test commands; no normalisation, no line joining), so block scalars, continued lines, chained commands or unknown steps are refused. tools/ops/verify-container.sh --fast-part <base|spec-i> runs one part from the trusted root in the --fast container and limits, records per-step start / end / exit code, takes its exit code from docker (a missing or malformed step record exits 2), and writes fast-part/<n>/ only (never verify-fast/). --fast is unchanged at run time (it only lists its steps in --dry-run). tools/ops/verify-sharded-summary.ts takes, per tree, the later of the whole verify-fast and a complete part group (each part matched to the current trusted part table by its recorded commands; int-shard segments likewise by their recorded command), green only when that evidence passed. Two README paragraphs. No money, ledger or attribution code touched.
